Rising cancer rates, a globalist agenda, and a corporate land grab are linked together in this Tucker Carlson episode. Carlson asks why cancer is striking younger people more often and who profits from widespread illness. He also turns to the soil, arguing big business is buying up the land under Americans' feet.

The episode moves from food and chemicals to farmland purchases by large firms and foreign buyers. Carlson frames sickness and land loss as two faces of the same system. He urges viewers to ask who gains from both trends. Concerned listeners get the host's case on health, soil, and power.
uslaw-usc-t2-s285c: Section 285c of Title 2 vests the running of the Office of Law Revision Counsel in one officer. The management, supervision, and administration of the Office are vested in the Law Revision Counsel. The Speaker appoints the Counsel, without regard to political affiliation and solely on the basis of fitness for the duties. The Counsel serves at the pleasure of the Speaker. The section sits in Chapter 9A of Title 2. The hosted Code text is current through Public Law 119-134.
